6. As against this Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that in the instant case, the impugned order is deemed to be a final order. In support of his contention, he cited two decisions as reported in AIR 1972 para 14, page 571 and 12 MLR (AD) 186 = 59 DLR (AD) 206. 

 10. On perusal of the aforesaid provisions, it is crystal clear that no order passed by any Court under this Act shall be questioned in the form of revision or an appeal in any higher Court. We have also gone through the decisions as cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, in the case of German D. Republic vs DIU Limited reported in AIR 1972 para 14 page-33 and Than Md Firoj Kabir vs Rupali Bank Limited reported in 12 MLR (AD) 186 = 59 DLR (AD) 206 respectively. We are of the view that the aforesaid two decisions are not applicable under the facts and circumstances of the instant case. Moreover, regarding this issue, we have earlier passed a decision in the case of Md Abdul Mannan Rouf vs Bangladesh Government as reported in 73 DLR 237.
